title: Priority curve and fallback contract for key accounts
creator: Jonah Rivera
description: Create a repeatable prioritization artefact that maps top-account signals to a graded commitment curve and an explicit fallback contract. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc escalations, give sales/CS predictable SLAs for roadmap delivery, and ensure engineering capacity planning can accept prioritized requests with a known runway and fallback policy.
background: We have many seat-of-the-pants commitments to top accounts that create risk for delivery and create cross-org confusion. Existing artifacts focus on admission criteria but do not define a quantifiable priority curve (how much runway and engineering commitment a given signal set buys) nor an agreed fallback (acceptable alternate delivery or SLA when runway or scope changes).
acceptance_criteria: A one-page Priority Curve visual that maps combined signals (ARR, deal stage, strategic fit, regression risk, security/compliance need) to 'Priority Tiers' and associated runway/commitment buckets
A 'Fallback Contract' template with two graded fallback options (de-scope, delayed scheduled delivery) and clear triggers for each
Operational owner and escalation path defined (PM, Eng lead, CS lead) with example run-throughs for 3 past escalations
An intake checkbox set added to the intake form used by CS to capture all signals required to compute the priority score
Pilot with 3 live accounts and retrospective showing reduced ambiguity in commitment and one concrete time/cost saving or avoided engineering disruption
stakeholders: Lars Becker - Eng Manager, Serving Runtime
proposed_workflow: Define signal taxonomy and weights (ARR, contract stage, product fit, compliance urgency, number of dependent features)
Design priority curve visualization and discrete Priority Tiers (P0-P3) with runway/commitment mapping
Draft Fallback Contract templates and acceptance criteria for each Tier
Integrate signal capture into existing intake form and compute a Priority Score automatically
Turn on pilot mode: CS/AM use the form for new requests; PM cadence to evaluate weekly; Eng capacity planner uses the Tier to reserve runway
Run 3 pilot cases end-to-end and produce retro + recommended tweaks
metrics: Time to decision on top-account intake (target < 72 hours)
% of escalations resolved with fallback contract invoked vs ad-hoc rework (target >= 70% using fallback)
Engineering schedule churn attributable to ad-hoc top-account changes (target decrease 30% in pilot group)
CS / Sales satisfaction with clarity of commitment (survey score target >= 4/5)
Number of commitments translated into roadmap items with explicit runway and owner
rollout_plan: Week 0-1: workshops with CS, Sales, Eng leads to finalize signals and weights
Week 2: design Priority Curve visual and Fallback Contract templates; instrument intake form
Week 3-6: pilot with 3 accounts, weekly alignment and capacity planning sync
Week 7: retrospective, iterate on thresholds and fallback language
Week 8: expand to top 25 accounts and bake into roadmap intake process
tradeoffs: Strict priority curves reduce flexibility for Sales, which could slow deal closures unless paired with clear fallback concessions
More conservative runway allocations will reduce short-term feature velocity for org but decrease firefighting overhead
Automating score computation risks misclassification if signal weights are incorrect; need manual overrides and audit logs

2025-02-25: Agreed on 3 Priority Tiers (Tier A: highest, Tier B: medium, Tier C: low) and that Tier A gets a 'reserved runway' window of 8 weeks - Priya Mehta
2025-03-03: Engineering requested a hard cap on Tier A concurrent runway claims to prevent capacity exhaustion; proposal to reserve 15% of sprint capacity for Tier A during pilot - Lars Becker
open_questions: What is the canonical source for ARR and contract stage signals (SFDC field mapping)?
How will we instrument audit logs for manual overrides of computed priority?
Do legal/finance need to sign off on fallback contract language for public cloud hosted customers?
What is the fallback compensation/discount policy when we de-scope or delay a contractual commitment?
